data.name: Chemically Bonded
data.detailed_description:
Check these out!



Acerca do jogo

Chemically Bonded


Enter the melancholic life of a Japanese high school student, as you soon become entwined in the dispute between two female students. Learn more about their past as you piece together their relationship and mend their bond, all whilst forming bonds of your own.

Players will be presented with both conventional and unconventional choices which shape the relationship formed with the girls. Help restart the Science club or choose to increase your athletic capabilities as you grow closer to she who holds the key to your heart.

Notice: Chemically Bonded is a work of fiction. Any resemblances to any persons, living or dead, or organisations are coincidental. All characters depicted in Chemically Bonded are over the age of 18.

Story

Between two girls' hearts lies a rift. One of misunderstanding, conflicting views and deceit. Each having a dream far too different from that of the other, but somehow keeping themselves ever so similar. Struggling to keep up with your own responsibilities, you stopped being a dreamer long ago. By chance, the lives of these two girls engrosses your world as you unwittingly form new bonds with them whilst trying to mend the broken ones they once held so dear. Maybe then, their dreams can come to fruition as you learn more about them and what matters the most to you.

Features:

  • Multiple routes and endings
  • Interactive phone system for choices and dates.
  • 5+ outfits and multiple poses for both girls.
  • High quality artwork.
  • Voice Acting
  • Genre: Romance, Drama, Comedy
  • Romance: B x G

Team*:

  • Scenario, Programming, UI: ds-sans
  • Original Artwork: Jun Project, mB0sco
  • Original Score: L. Dougherty, Red Robotix
  • Main Heroine VAs: N i i, Amber Barile
    * Full cast and credits available in-game.

    Frequent updates on the project can be found on twitter @dssansVN



    Kiyoko Ishikawa (CV: N i i)

    As an aspiring scientist, Kiyoko prides herself on her ability to control her emotions through the use of logic. At least, that's what she believes. Despite having an overly emotive personality, she's often mistaken for the quiet type despite having a lot to say. Her inquisitive nature usually leads to chaos, as despite enjoying an experiment or two she has no concern for health and safety procedures. Kiyoko is the founder and currently sole member of the science club and tends to keep to herself, being known around the school for her outstanding intellect.

    Naomi Satō (CV: Amber Barile)

    Naomi is a girl with plenty of passion, most of which she puts into her attitude. Extremely popular, even to those of the same sex. She isn't afraid of conversation, however despite her popularity her social circle is quite limited. She is the captain of the athletics team when she isn't having her say over every sporting club in the school. She'd be considered a tomboy by most outsiders, but those who know her well are privy to her innermost girlish quirks.

reviews.review:
Chemically Bonded is an indie visual novel developed and published by ds-sans that builds its experience around romance, school life, and the complexities of repairing damaged friendships. Rather than aiming for an epic narrative, the game focuses on a smaller and more personal story, placing players in the shoes of a high school student who finds himself caught between two girls whose relationship has deteriorated over time. The premise immediately establishes a familiar anime-inspired atmosphere, blending lighthearted moments with emotional drama while inviting players to shape the outcome through their choices.

At the center of the story are Kiyoko and Naomi, two characters with contrasting personalities that drive much of the narrative. Kiyoko's enthusiasm for science and optimistic outlook stand in stark contrast to Naomi's more reserved and stubborn demeanor. Their strained friendship serves as the emotional backbone of the game, giving players a reason to invest in their interactions beyond simple romantic pursuits. While the character archetypes are recognizable to anyone familiar with visual novels, the writing succeeds in making their conflicts feel genuine enough to carry the experience. The game places considerable emphasis on conversations and interpersonal moments, allowing players to gradually uncover each character's motivations and aspirations.

One of the more interesting additions is the in-game smartphone system, which lets players communicate with the heroines, schedule outings, and influence their relationships outside of the main story scenes. Combined with multiple routes and endings, this mechanic gives the experience a greater sense of involvement than a purely linear visual novel. Choices matter throughout the adventure, and although the branching paths are not dramatically different from one another, they offer enough variation to encourage multiple playthroughs. Additional activities, including involvement with the Science Club and other aspects of school life, help flesh out the setting and make the world feel more active.

The presentation is arguably one of Chemically Bonded's greatest strengths. Character sprites are expressive and detailed, while special event illustrations effectively highlight major emotional and romantic moments. The visual design remains consistently polished throughout the game's relatively short runtime, helping maintain player engagement even during slower scenes. Despite being an independently developed title with limited resources, it demonstrates a commendable level of care in its artistic direction. The user interface is straightforward and easy to navigate, ensuring that players can focus entirely on the story without unnecessary distractions.

Sound design further enhances the experience. The soundtrack delivers a pleasant mix of upbeat and reflective pieces that fit the game's tone, while voice acting adds personality to the cast. Although some performances are stronger than others, the inclusion of voiced dialogue contributes significantly to the immersion and elevates the production beyond what many small visual novels attempt. The music does an excellent job of supporting the narrative's emotional beats, particularly during scenes involving reconciliation and personal reflection.

Chemically Bonded does not reinvent the visual novel genre, nor does it attempt to challenge its conventions. Instead, it embraces them wholeheartedly, offering a concise and heartfelt experience that will likely appeal most to fans of anime-inspired romance stories. Its pacing occasionally moves too quickly, and some character developments could have benefited from additional time and depth. However, the game's sincerity and attention to presentation help overcome many of these shortcomings.

For players seeking a lengthy or highly complex narrative, Chemically Bonded may feel modest in scope. However, those looking for a comfortable and emotionally driven visual novel will find an experience that is easy to appreciate. It is a game that understands its audience and delivers exactly what it promises: a charming story about friendship, love, and the bonds people struggle to preserve as they grow older.

Rating: 7/10
